# KMP feasibility harness

Standalone probes for dependency compatibility, common-test discovery and the
complete embedded dictionary payload, controlled seeded sampling and portable
regex generation. See [feasibility evidence](../../../../docs/feat/wip/kotlin-multiplatform/feasibility.md).
This build is not included in the production project or release/BOM graph.

From the repository root, with JDK 21 installed:

```sh
./gradlew -p test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility inventoryInputs jvmTest jsNodeTest randomCoverageVerification regexCoverageVerification
./gradlew -p test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility jsBrowserTest
./gradlew -p test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility jvmTest -PprobeTestJdk=11
```

The browser test requires Chrome; the JVM 11 command requires a discoverable
JDK 11. On an Arm64 Mac with Xcode 26.0.1 and an available iOS simulator:

```sh
./gradlew -p test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility iosSimulatorArm64Test linkDebugTestIosArm64
```

`-PprobeKotlinVersion=2.3.20` selects the provisional lower compiler for API
compatibility experiments. Keep failed runs as evidence; do not use metadata
version bypass flags. The independent `consumer/` build pins Kotlin 2.3.20 and
consumes artifacts produced by the default Kotlin 2.3.21 build.

Reports are under `build/test-results/` and `build/inventory/`. The inventory
uses the production SnakeYAML/ICU versions, expands YAML aliases and records
non-string scalars/keys rather than normalizing them away. Regex rows use `0` and
`A` for randomized placeholders; they describe syntax after preprocessing.

`generatePayload` runs automatically before common-source compilation. It writes
category projections and a source/locale/overlay manifest to generated Kotlin
under `build/generated/payload/commonMain/`. Never edit or commit those outputs.
Literal chunks are limited to 8,000 UTF-16 units and 24,000 JVM modified-UTF-8
bytes without splitting surrogate pairs; supplier methods avoid constant folding
and oversized initializers. The accessor decodes and caches only the requested
physical source/category. It does not resolve locale fallback or expressions.

Shared tests compare every projection with its pre-compilation UTF-16 length
and 64-bit FNV-1a fingerprint, round-trip it, and check lazy decoding, aliases,
Unicode, metadata and existing Boolean coercions. The JVM test independently
converts all authoring YAML and reconstructs it from the compiled projections,
checking every scalar, key and array position. Object key order is canonicalized.
Fingerprint expectations are generated under `commonTest`, so verification
metadata does not enlarge the main library artifact. Golden vectors check the
UTF-16 fingerprint implementation, including surrogate pairs and escaped text.
The `no` root and Spanish `NO` scalar remain `false`, exactly as in the current
production conversion; the manifest keeps logical filename locale separately.
Source-kind ranks classify locale-wide, primary and secondary files. Selection
and merging belong to Task 5: in particular, default English selects a secondary
resource instead of overlaying it on a primary resource.

After compiling targets, run `measurePayloadArtifacts` to produce
`build/payload-artifacts.tsv`. Generation sizes and a reproducible source hash
are in `build/generated/payload/manifest.json`. Use `--profile` for Gradle task
timings. Hosted runs also retain `/usr/bin/time` output; its maximum RSS is a
process measurement, not a sum of simultaneous compiler/browser memory.

No production facade, provider, fallback resolver or uniqueness implementation
belongs here.

`probe.random` contains independent raw-word and sampling components. Common tests
use fixed vectors plus scripted words for rejection boundaries and exact bit/byte
consumption. Reproduce the offline reference vectors with
`python3 test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility/random_reference.py` from the repository root.
That Python script uses arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic and never imports
or runs the Kotlin implementation. The fixed vectors are not regenerated by Gradle.
`randomCoverageVerification` enforces 100% JVM line/branch coverage for the two
handwritten random classes; XML/HTML reports are in `build/reports/jacoco/`.
See [Task 25's specification](../../../../docs/feat/wip/kotlin-multiplatform/feasibility.md#task-25-controlled-seeded-operations)
for bounds, seed mapping, word consumption and promotion limits.

`probe.regex` parses and validates the entire pattern before using that sampler.
Its grammar includes literal/Unicode text, classes, groups, alternatives, root
anchors and bounded repetition, with a fixed cap for `*` and `+`. Unsupported
syntax fails with a position/reason before consuming randomness. Output, pattern,
alphabet, nesting and expansion-work limits are explicit in
[Task 3's grammar](../../../../docs/feat/wip/kotlin-multiplatform/feasibility.md#task-3-portable-regex-generation).

The common corpus tests classify and exercise every inventoried pattern from the
embedded dictionaries. JVM tests compare every occurrence with Task 1's inventory;
`jvmTest` builds that inventory automatically. Independent choice vectors are
reproducible with `python3 test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility/regex_reference.py`.
`regexCoverageVerification` enforces 100% JVM line/branch coverage for the handwritten
regex mechanism; both coverage reports are under `build/reports/jacoco/`.

## Published probe consumer

The sole probe module publishes root metadata and target artifacts as
`io.github.serpro69.kfaker.probe:kfaker-kmp-feasibility:0.0.0-local` to
`build/probe-repository/`. This is a file repository, outside production includes,
the BOM and release aggregation. No remote repository or signing is configured.

On Linux, stage the root/JVM/JS publications and run the independent consumer:

```sh
./gradlew -p test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility clean publishKotlinMultiplatformPublicationToProbeRepository publishJvmPublicationToProbeRepository publishJsPublicationToProbeRepository
./gradlew -p test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility/consumer jvmTest jsNodeTest jsBrowserTest boundaryCoverageVerification
./gradlew -p test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility/consumer jvmTest -PprobeTestJdk=11
```

On the supported Arm64 Mac, stage every publication and execute/link the consumer.
The explicit common metadata compilation needs all declared target publications,
including iOS, so it runs against this complete repository:

```sh
./gradlew -p test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility clean publishAllPublicationsToProbeRepository
./gradlew -p test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility/consumer compileCommonMainKotlinMetadata iosSimulatorArm64Test linkDebugTestIosArm64
```

The consumer declares the coordinates in `commonMain`, with no producer sources,
project substitutions or Maven Local fallback. Maven Central excludes the probe
group. It checks every payload projection against a fixed aggregate of Task 2's
pre-compilation expectations, round-trips the decoded data, observes lazy counts,
and checks seeded random/regex vectors and failure behavior. Ordinary build-tool
and runtime-library downloads are needed for an uncached build; generation itself
is synchronous and offline, with no dictionary download or asset setup.

The consumer compiler stays at 2.3.20. Published dependency metadata requests
stdlib 2.3.21 on JVM/JS; this differs from the earlier source-only 2.3.20 probe.
Native uses the compiler's bundled stdlib. Production floors must still be checked
against actual core/domain publications in Tasks 29/21.

`boundaryCoverageVerification` measures the resolved JVM artifact's probe facade
and the consumer's common entry point, requiring 100% line/branch coverage. It
does not use producer class directories. Existing mechanism coverage remains in
the producer. JS/iOS are behavioral checks, not measured coverage claims.
The workflow retains named consumer XML, dependency graphs, common/device task
logs, publication metadata and file sizes/hashes. See the Task 4 section in
`feasibility.md` for the decision, evidence and remaining production gates.

To reproduce the consumer's fixed payload fingerprint after `generatePayload`,
run this standalone Python reference from the repository root. It reads the
pre-compilation expectations, not the compiled artifact being tested. Dictionary
changes require reviewing the source-fidelity results before updating the golden
value; the script never rewrites the consumer test.

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

root = Path('test/fixtures/kmp-feasibility/build/generated/payload/commonTest')
parts = sorted(root.glob('generatedExpectationsPart*.kt'),
               key=lambda p: int(re.search(r'Part(\d+)', p.name)[1]))
assert parts, 'Run generatePayload first'
rows = []
for part in parts:
    entries = re.findall(r'PayloadExpectation\(("[^"]+"), (null|"[^"]+"), (\d+), 0x([a-f0-9]+)uL\)', part.read_text())
    assert entries, part
    for path, category, length, checksum in entries:
        category = '-' if category == 'null' else json.loads(category)
        rows.append(f'{json.loads(path)}\t{category}\t{length}\t{int(checksum, 16):016x}\n')
hash_value = 0xcbf29ce484222325
for char in ''.join(rows):
    hash_value = ((hash_value ^ ord(char)) * 0x100000001b3) & ((1 << 64) - 1)
print(f'{len(rows)} projections: {hash_value:016x}')
PY
```

The current result is `666 projections: 14376e443dcf410f`. Consumer seed-0 and
seed-minus-one values come from `random_reference.py` and the corresponding
`RandomSamplingTest` vectors: raw seed-minus-one word `e4d971771b652c20` is signed
Long `-1956407806741107680`. Regex choices come from `regex_reference.py` and
`PortableRegexTest`; these are test oracles, not copied generator implementations.
